name: Oral testosterone undecanoate (Jatenzo / Kyzatrex)

card.summary: Prescription capsules that deliver testosterone by mouth for diagnosed deficiency; a medical TRT option, not a studied looksmaxxing tool.
card.note: US labels for oral testosterone undecanoate products carry blood pressure warnings; prescription-only controlled substance.

quick.overview:
Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription capsule form of testosterone replacement therapy. Jatenzo was approved by the US FDA in 2019 as the first oral version, followed by Tlando and Kyzatrex in 2022. It is approved for adult men with low or absent testosterone from specific medical causes.

In looksmaxxing and muscle-focused communities it is discussed mainly as a needle-free alternative to injectable or gel TRT. No published trials examine it for appearance or muscle-building in healthy men.
quick.mechanism: Testosterone undecanoate is a prodrug of testosterone. Ordinary oral testosterone is largely cleared by the liver, so these capsules use a lipid-based formulation intended to carry the compound through the lymphatic system and avoid this first-pass loss. Absorption is reported to rise with fatty food and to vary between individuals.
quick.risks: Reported effects include raised blood pressure, acne, hair growth, raised liver enzymes and lipid changes. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and requires a prescription. Testosterone products in general can suppress sperm production.

lead: Oral testosterone undecanoate is a testosterone replacement therapy taken by mouth as a capsule. Testosterone undecanoate is a prodrug of testosterone, meaning it is converted to the active hormone in the body [1]. Brand names include Jatenzo, Kyzatrex and Tlando in the United States, and Andriol elsewhere [1][2].

The US Food and Drug Administration approved Jatenzo in March 2019 as the first oral testosterone undecanoate product, with Tlando approved in March 2022 and Kyzatrex in July 2022 [1]. These products are indicated for adult men with testosterone deficiency from defined medical conditions rather than for age-related decline or cosmetic purposes [1].

Within appearance and muscle-oriented communities, oral TRT is discussed as an alternative to injections or gels. No published trials have tested it in healthy men for physique or facial appearance outcomes. The only registered trial in the available record is an early-phase study in menopausal women with low sexual desire [3].

paras: The approved use is testosterone replacement in adult men with low or absent endogenous testosterone [1]. Wikipedia's overview of testosterone medications lists oral undecanoate among several delivery options alongside injections, gels, patches and implants [2].

Plain oral testosterone is extensively metabolised by the liver on first pass, so its oral bioavailability is very low [2]. Undecanoate esters are reported to have bioavailability of roughly 3 to 7 percent that improves with fatty meals, with a short oral half-life of about 1.6 hours and wide variation between individuals [1]. By contrast, the intramuscular undecanoate depot has a half-life measured in weeks [1].

Reported effects of testosterone undecanoate include acne, increased body hair, voice changes in women, hypertension, raised liver enzymes and raised triglycerides [1]. In February 2025 the FDA was reported to have removed cardiovascular-event language from the boxed warning for testosterone products while adding a warning about increased blood pressure [2]. Exogenous testosterone can suppress sperm production, sometimes reversibly [2].

Ciba filed patents on a related testosterone undecylenate combination in the mid-1950s, and oral undecanoate use began in Europe in the late 1970s [1]. US approval of an oral version came only in 2019, followed by two further products in 2022 [1].
Testosterone undecanoate is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and Schedule IV in Canada, and is available by prescription only [1].

No studies found examining oral testosterone undecanoate for appearance or physique in healthy men. A registered open-label phase 2 study (NCT06082817) plans to test a 50 mg Kyzatrex regimen in 30 menopausal women with low testosterone and hypoactive sexual desire disorder; it was listed as not yet recruiting [3].

timeline.event: Ciba files Swiss patents on a related testosterone undecylenate combination [1].
Injectable undecanoate (Nebido) first approved in Europe [1].
FDA approves Jatenzo, the first oral testosterone undecanoate [1].
Tlando (March) and Kyzatrex (July) approved by the FDA [1].
